Reference

Both source photos this build was authored against. Note: the primary is an oblique 3/4 shot, not orthographic — see the measurement note below before reading any silhouette number as absolute.

Model views

Material-lit renders of the current committed state (decision_revision 13). Front and side are true orthographic; the third is an oblique angle matching the reference's own framing.

Surface and construction evidence

MatCap isolates shading defects a flat render can hide; wireframe shows the actual topology behind the shading, not just a smooth surface.

Measured comparison

Silhouette metrics, front view, uniform-bbox alignment against the primary reference. Today's chamfer and socket work correctly left these flat — neither change touches the outer silhouette.

The negative-space gap concentrates at the shackle opening. Deliberately not "fixed" by narrowing the shackle: the current leg spacing (21mm clearance) reproduces the official spec exactly, and the reference photo is labeled PERSPECTIVE, not orthographic — narrowing a dimensionally-anchored part to fit a perspective-distorted photo would trade a verified measurement for a worse one.

Known uncertainties

Open by design, not by oversight — none of these are silently assumed away.

  • Rear and underside geometryNo source establishes them; the reference set only covers front/oblique angles. Not modeled, not guessed.
  • "Master" wordmark and front seam detailThe seam recess is built; the engraved text is not. Deliberately deferred until primary form is accepted, per this build's own construction log.
  • Negative-space gap at the shackle openingMeasured, not fixed — see the comparison note above. Would need a true orthogonal front photo to tell shape error from perspective artifact with confidence.
  • No formal stage-gate trackingThis build predates blender_ops/modeling_stage.py and has no _modeling_stage property — tracked only through this run's dated commits and README.

Review questions

Answer inline as a comment on this artifact, or reply in chat — either becomes the review record.

  1. Does it read as the same object as the reference?
  2. Is the body's overall proportion (width / depth / height) correct?Depth (16mm) is the least-certain dimension — photo-derived, not spec'd.
  3. Is the shackle arch shape and thickness correct?
  4. Is the body-to-shackle size relationship correct?
  5. Do the shackle sockets read as a real construction detail, not a defect?
  6. Does the front corner chamfer look proportioned right, or too subtle / too heavy?
  7. Is the side depth believable at this angle?
  8. Any major form that's obviously wrong, independent of the above?
